review::.::holistic::cross_module_archit.summary: Save/export workflow for the four non-character card types is copied into four editors with no owning lib module

evidence: exportPng() in ScriptEditor.tsx:65-74, ScenarioEditor.tsx:68-77 and PersonaEditor.tsx:75-84 are byte-identical apart from the card-type string passed to encodeCharaToPng; LoreBookEditor.tsx:208-217 differs only in serialising buildExportData() instead of `card`.

handleSaveToLibrary() in the same four files repeats the same version-changed / saveAnyCard / setLibraryId / setSavedVersion / status-message sequence (ScriptEditor.tsx:76-86, ScenarioEditor.tsx:79-89, PersonaEditor.tsx:86-96, LoreBookEditor.tsx:219-230), including the identical three-way success message.

The same four-way fan-out reappears twice more: App.tsx:47-69 declares four parallel {key, init} state pairs and App.tsx:168-215 eight near-identical handlers, and src/lib/bridge/client.ts:222-241 switches over the same five card types again.

src/lib/library/index.ts exposes saveCard (character) and saveAnyCard (everything else) as separate entry points, so the character export path in CardPreviewPanel.tsx is a fifth copy of the same encode-and-download sequence.
detail.suggestion: Add one module, src/lib/simpleCard.ts, owning the non-character card workflow: `exportSimpleCardPng(cardType, body, imageSrc, fileName)` (carrier PNG + encodeCharaToPng + downloadPng) and `saveSimpleCard(cardType, name, body, imageSrc, tags, libraryId, versionChanged)` returning the saved LibraryCard. Have the four editors call those two functions instead of holding their own copies. That is one new file replacing eight duplicated function bodies, so net complexity drops; do not add a generic editor component or a card-type registry on top of it.

review::.::holistic::cross_module_archit.summary: protocol.ts re-declares CardType identically to LibraryCardType and the two are joined by unchecked casts

evidence: src/lib/bridge/protocol.ts:97 declares `export type CardType = "character" | "lorebook" | "script" | "scenario" | "persona";` and src/types/index.ts:163 declares LibraryCardType with the same five members.

src/lib/bridge/client.ts converts between them with four unchecked assertions: `cardType: c.cardType as CardType` at lines 281 and 313, and `cardType: saved.cardType as CardType` at lines 360 and 374.

src/lib/bridge/client.ts:350 then maintains a third copy of the same list as a runtime ALLOWED_CARD_TYPES array. Adding a sixth card type to types/index.ts would compile cleanly while the bridge silently rejected or mistyped it.
detail.suggestion: The duplication itself is justified (protocol.ts must stay dependency-free for the mcp package), but the drift should be compile-checked. In src/lib/bridge/client.ts, which already imports both, add one line next to the imports: `type _CardTypeParity = [LibraryCardType] extends [CardType] ? ([CardType] extends [LibraryCardType] ? true : never) : never;` and drop the four `as CardType` casts so the mismatch surfaces at the cast sites instead. One line added, four casts removed.

review::.::holistic::cross_module_archit.summary: mcp/tsconfig.json declares only half the app modules the MCP package actually imports, and nothing enforces their browser-neutrality

evidence: mcp/tsconfig.json's include list is ["src/**/*.ts", "../src/lib/bridge/protocol.ts", "../src/lib/personaParser/index.ts"], but mcp/src/index.ts:24-25 also imports ../../src/lib/validators/index.js and ../../src/lib/platforms/index.js.

The include list reads as the declaration of which app modules the Node package is allowed to reach into (README.md documents mcp/ as 'own package; shares src/lib'), so it is a documented contract that has drifted from what the code does.

mcp/tsconfig.json sets lib to ["ES2022", "DOM"], so a browser-only API added to any of those four shared modules would typecheck in the MCP package and only fail at runtime; there are no tests over mcp/src to catch it either.
detail.suggestion: Add the two missing entries to mcp/tsconfig.json's include list so it names the full shared surface (../src/lib/validators/index.ts and ../src/lib/platforms/index.ts), and add a one-line comment in mcp/src/index.ts above the ../../src imports stating that only browser-neutral modules may be imported there. Single-file edit, no new structure.

review::.::holistic::high_level_elegance.summary: Lorebook/Script/Scenario/Persona editors each re-implement the same card-editor lifecycle; no module owns it

evidence: All four hold the identical state set — card, imageSrc, libraryId, saving, savedVersion, outputFileName — plus the same useEffect syncing outputFileName to card.name with a per-kind suffix (ScenarioEditor.tsx:34-48, PersonaEditor.tsx:42-49, ScriptEditor.tsx:38-45, LoreBookEditor.tsx:105-113).

exportPng is the same four lines in each (getCarrierPng(imageSrc) -> JSON.stringify -> encodeCharaToPng(bytes, json, "<kind>", false) -> downloadPng), and handleSaveToLibrary is the same versionChanged/saveAnyCard/status-message block with only the kind string and 'Unnamed X' label differing (ScenarioEditor.tsx:66-89 vs PersonaEditor.tsx:75-95 vs ScriptEditor.tsx:65-85 vs LoreBookEditor.tsx:208-228).
The character card does none of this: its state lives in App.tsx and its export/save live in CardPreviewPanel.tsx, so the same domain concept has two unrelated ownership models.
App.tsx mirrors the duplication with four <kind>Init/<kind>Key state pairs and eight handleEdit*/handleImport* callbacks that differ only in which setter they call (App.tsx:50-208).
detail.suggestion: Extract one useCardEditor hook into src/hooks (e.g. useCardEditor(kind, defaultCard)) that owns card/imageSrc/libraryId/saving/savedVersion/outputFileName plus update, clearForNew, exportJson, exportPng and saveToLibrary, parameterised by a small per-kind descriptor { metadataKey, fileSuffix, unnamedLabel } kept next to the card-type union. The four editors then keep only their form JSX. This is a net reduction: one owner and one descriptor table replace four copies of the same lifecycle.

review::.::holistic::high_level_elegance.summary: The five-member card-type vocabulary is redeclared in five modules and cast between, so no module owns it

evidence: Identical unions: LibraryCardType (src/types/index.ts:163), CardType (src/lib/bridge/protocol.ts:97), CardShape (src/lib/cardShape.ts:13), DetectedType (src/components/ImportPNG.tsx:10), NonCharType (src/components/DecodePNG.tsx:13).

src/lib/bridge/client.ts bridges the split with casts rather than types: `cardType: c.cardType as CardType` at lines 281, 312, 360, 374 and `existing.cardType as CardType` at line 367 — the duplication costs real type checking at exactly the app/agent boundary.

The vocabulary owner is already drifting: LibraryCard.rawData in src/types/index.ts is documented as 'present when cardType is lorebook | script | scenario', omitting persona, which has been a card type since the persona editor landed.
Adding a sixth card type today means editing five unions, ALLOWED_CARD_TYPES in client.ts:350, TYPE_ORDER in Library.tsx:34, and a fifth onLoad* callback threaded through App/ImportPNG/DecodePNG.
detail.suggestion: Make src/types/index.ts the sole owner: keep LibraryCardType there, have cardShape.ts export `type CardShape = LibraryCardType` (or import it directly), replace DetectedType/NonCharType in ImportPNG/DecodePNG with the shared type, and either alias protocol.ts's CardType to LibraryCardType (mcp/tsconfig.json already compiles files from ../src) or add a one-line comment saying it is a deliberately frozen wire type. Then delete the five `as CardType` casts in bridge/client.ts.

review::.::holistic::high_level_elegance.summary: The blank character card exists twice — in lib/tavernCard.ts and in the Ronan Voss template file the app actually uses

evidence: src/lib/tavernCard.ts documents createBlankTavernCard() as 'An empty, spec-valid Tavern Card v2 — the starting shape for every import path', and converters.ts and bridge/client.ts do use it.

src/data/templates/ronalVoss.ts:42 declares blankTemplate with a byte-identical body, and App.tsx imports that one for both the initial project state (line 41) and clearCard (line 155) — so the editor's own start is the one path the documented origin does not cover.
The same character-named file also owns the template registry (`templates`, line 63) consumed by Templates.tsx, so 'where do built-in templates live' resolves to a file named after one of them.
detail.suggestion: Delete blankTemplate and have both ronalVoss.ts's registry entry and App.tsx call createBlankTavernCard(); then rename src/data/templates/ronalVoss.ts to src/data/templates/index.ts (keeping the ronanVossTemplate constant inside it) so the registry's location matches its role. Fewer definitions, one origin, no new abstraction.

review::.::holistic::high_level_elegance.summary: personaParser/personaLlm are named for a persona-only past but now own text parsing for every card type

evidence: src/lib/personaParser/index.ts:36 declares `export type PersonaField = CardField` with the comment 'Historical alias — the parser started out persona-only', and the module exports both PERSONA_FIELDS and CHARACTER_FIELDS plus toCharacterFields().
src/lib/personaLlm/index.ts takes a SortTarget of 'persona' | 'character' and is driven from SmartImportPanel in both the Character and Persona editors.
mcp/src/index.ts exposes the same module to agents under the accurate name parse_card_text, so the public tool name and the module name already disagree.
detail.suggestion: Rename the two directories to src/lib/cardTextParser and src/lib/cardTextSorter (or textSorter), drop the PersonaField alias in favour of CardField, and update the ~10 import sites. Purely mechanical, and it makes the directory listing describe what the modules do rather than what they used to do.

review::.::holistic::high_level_elegance.summary: minimalPng.ts claims a minimalPng.test.ts verifies its bytes; that test does not exist

evidence: src/lib/minimalPng.ts:7 states 'every CRC validates, and the stream ends exactly on IEND. `minimalPng.test.ts` re-checks all of that.'

The repo's only test files are src/lib/cardShape.test.ts, src/lib/personaParser/index.test.ts, src/lib/platforms/converters.test.ts and src/lib/pngMetadata/index.test.ts — the cited guard is missing, and the same header records that a previously malformed constant corrupted every art-less export.
detail.suggestion: Either add the small src/lib/minimalPng.test.ts the comment promises (walk the chunk lengths, verify each CRC, assert the stream ends on IEND) or delete that sentence. Given the regression it describes, adding the test is the better of the two.

review::.::holistic::convention_outlier:.summary: DecodePNG classifies cards by metadata keyword alone and re-declares CHARACTER_KEYS, while ImportPNG uses lib/cardShape

evidence: src/lib/cardShape.ts exports CHARACTER_KEYS, shapeForKey and detectCardShape, and its docstring records the bug it was written for: trusting the PNG keyword rebuilt a mislabelled lorebook as a blank character card and dropped every entry.

src/components/DecodePNG.tsx:11 declares its own `const CHARACTER_KEYS = new Set(["chara", "character", "tavern", "tavern_card_v2"])` — a verbatim copy of the exported Set — and never imports lib/cardShape.

DecodePNG's processFile (lines 74-80) and handleLoadToEditor (lines 106-119) branch only on the metadata `key`, so a lorebook stored under `chara` is labelled a character card and handed to convertCardFrom, exactly the failure ImportPNG.tsx (lines 88-95) guards against with `const actual = detectCardShape(parsed)` and its mismatch note.
detail.suggestion: In src/components/DecodePNG.tsx, delete the local CHARACTER_KEYS and import { CHARACTER_KEYS, shapeForKey, detectCardShape } from "../lib/cardShape"; compute the effective shape the way ImportPNG does (shape wins over keyword on mismatch) and switch both processFile's format label and handleLoadToEditor's dispatch onto that shape instead of result.key.

review::.::holistic::convention_outlier:.summary: Bridge openCard preserves the library id for characters but routes the other four card types through id-less import handlers

evidence: src/App.tsx:224-241: the registerBridgeHost openCard switch calls loadFromLibrary(card.cardData, null, image, card.id) for "character" but handleImportLorebook/Script/Scenario/Persona(card.rawData, image) for the other four — those handlers set `{ card, imageSrc }` with no id, unlike the sibling handleEditLorebook/Script/Scenario/Persona (lines 166-189) which pass the id through.
src/lib/bridge/client.ts:359 and 373 pass the freshly saved LibraryCard — id included — to host.openCard, so the id is available for every type.

With initialLibraryId undefined the editor's handleSaveToLibrary calls saveAnyCard(..., undefined), and src/lib/library/index.ts:71 then mints `crypto.randomUUID()`, so saving an agent-opened lorebook creates a duplicate entry; the button also reads "Save to Library" rather than "Update in Library".
detail.suggestion: In App.tsx's openCard switch, call the identity-preserving handlers for the non-character cases — handleEditLorebook(card.rawData as LoreBook, image, card.id) and the Script/Scenario/Persona equivalents — so all five branches follow the same protocol.

review::.::holistic::convention_outlier:.summary: useUnsavedWarning guards character editing only; the four sibling editors hold the same unsaved React state without it

evidence: useUnsavedWarning has exactly one call site, src/App.tsx:90, gated on character-card fields (project.card.data.name/description/personality/first_mes).

PersonaEditor, ScenarioEditor, ScriptEditor and LoreBookEditor each keep their card in `useState` until handleSaveToLibrary or an export runs — the same situation the hook's docstring describes ('whatever is in an editor is plain React state until you hit Save to Library or export'), yet none of them import the hook.
detail.suggestion: Call useUnsavedWarning in each of the four editors with a dirty check on their own state (e.g. in PersonaEditor: useUnsavedWarning(!libraryId && !!card.name.trim())), matching the character path's gating.

review::.::holistic::convention_outlier:.summary: ScriptEditor's CodeEditor is styled with inline hex colours while all other components use the semantic Tailwind tokens

evidence: src/components/ScriptEditor.tsx lines 265-340 set background/color/border through inline style objects with raw values (#1a1d2e, #7a8aaa, #a78bfa, #c8d3f5, #3d4a6b, rgba(100,110,160,0.2)) across the wrapper, header, gutter and textarea.

tailwind.config.js defines the app's colour vocabulary (bg.*, text.*, status.*, border.*) with a comment instructing that these be used instead of raw palette values; every other component styles via those classes, with inline `style` reserved for computed values such as progress-bar widths (CardPreviewPanel.tsx:271, 303).
detail.suggestion: Add the code-surface colours to the existing `colors` block in tailwind.config.js (e.g. a `code: { bg, gutter, text, chrome }` group) and replace CodeEditor's inline style objects with the corresponding className utilities, keeping inline style only for the computed gutter line height.

review::.::holistic::convention_outlier:.summary: The same five card kinds are declared as four separately named unions, forcing casts between structurally identical types

evidence: LibraryCardType (src/types/index.ts:163), CardShape (src/lib/cardShape.ts:13), CardType (src/lib/bridge/protocol.ts:97) and DetectedType (src/components/ImportPNG.tsx:10) all spell out "character" | "lorebook" | "script" | "scenario" | "persona".
src/lib/bridge/client.ts writes `c.cardType as CardType` eight times (lines 281, 312, 321, 350, 360, 367, 374) purely to cross between two of these identical aliases.
src/components/DecodePNG.tsx:13 adds a fifth, NonCharType, for the same set minus "character".
detail.suggestion: Keep LibraryCardType in src/types as the single declaration; make CardShape and CardType aliases of it (`export type CardType = LibraryCardType`) — protocol.ts must stay dependency-light, so if that import is unwanted, at minimum drop DetectedType and NonCharType in favour of LibraryCardType / Exclude<LibraryCardType, "character">. The casts in bridge/client.ts then disappear.

review::.::holistic::convention_outlier:.summary: src/lib mixes single-file directories with flat files of the same size, with no visible rule separating the two

evidence: archive/, customTemplates/, library/, tokenizer/, validators/ and personaParser/ each contain only index.ts (plus, for two of them, a colocated test), while download.ts (35 LOC), settings.ts, cardShape.ts, carrierImage.ts, readImageFile.ts, minimalPng.ts and tavernCard.ts sit flat — archive/index.ts is 47 LOC, larger than several of the flat files.
The multi-file directories are themselves inconsistent: platforms/ and personaLlm/ have an index.ts entry point, bridge/ (client.ts + protocol.ts) has none.
detail.suggestion: Flatten the single-file directories to plain modules (src/lib/archive.ts, customTemplates.ts, library.ts, tokenizer.ts, validators.ts, personaParser.ts) so directories mean 'more than one file'; import paths are unchanged in specifier text apart from the module name, and the tree loses six directories. review::.::holistic::low_level_elegance:.summary: deleteEntry mixes a functional updater with a stale outer read and picks an arbitrary survivor

The immediately following toggleEnabled carries the comment "Use functional updater to avoid stale-closure on book.entries", so the hazard was already recognised one function later.

review::.::holistic::low_level_elegance:.summary: getCardTokenBreakdown declares nine locals and hand-sums them; the 3000 ceiling is restated in the UI

detail.suggestion: Build the breakdown from a `COUNTED_FIELDS` list and derive total with a single reduce, keeping alternate_greetings as the one special case; export the 3000 ceiling as `TOKEN_BUDGET_MAX` from the tokenizer and import it in CardPreviewPanel instead of the local MAX_TOKENS.

review::.::holistic::mid_level_elegance:.summary: DecodePNG routes payloads by metadata key with its own CHARACTER_KEYS copy, ignoring lib/cardShape

evidence: DecodePNG.tsx line 11 re-declares `const CHARACTER_KEYS = new Set(["chara","character","tavern","tavern_card_v2"])`, which src/lib/cardShape.ts already exports.

handleLoadToEditor (DecodePNG.tsx ~line 108) dispatches on `result.key` alone: `if (result.key === "lorebook")` etc., never calling detectCardShape. cardShape.ts's own header documents the bug this causes — a lorebook exported under the `chara` key gets rebuilt as a blank character card — and ImportPNG.tsx lines 90-94 fixes it via `shapeForKey` + `detectCardShape` + mismatch reconciliation.
uint8ToDataUrl is defined twice: module scope in ImportPNG.tsx line 36, inline inside processFile in DecodePNG.tsx line 54.
detail.suggestion: In DecodePNG.tsx, delete the local CHARACTER_KEYS and the inline uint8ToDataUrl; import CHARACTER_KEYS (or shapeForKey) and detectCardShape from ../lib/cardShape, compute the effective shape once in processFile alongside the existing detection, store it on `result`, and have handleLoadToEditor switch on that shape instead of result.key. Export uint8ToDataUrl from a shared module (src/lib/readImageFile.ts is the natural home) and import it in both components.

review::.::holistic::mid_level_elegance:.summary: Lorebook normalisation lives inside LoreBookEditor, so PNG and bridge imports pass raw payloads through an `as LoreBook` cast

evidence: parseSillyTavernLorebook (LoreBookEditor.tsx line 50) is the only code that copes with object-keyed entries, missing entry ids, and comment/name aliasing, and it is called from exactly one place — the editor's own JSON drop handler (line 152).
ImportPNG.tsx passes `parsed as LoreBook` to onLoadLorebook, and App.tsx's bridge openCard passes `card.rawData as LoreBook`; both land directly in `useState<LoreBook>(initialBook ?? DEFAULT_BOOK)`.

detectCardShape treats an object-valued `entries` as a lorebook (cardShape.ts hasEntries), and LoreBookEditor then calls book.entries.map / .length / .find (lines 234, 308, 313), so that payload throws instead of importing.
MCP create_lorebook (mcp/src/index.ts ~line 205) fills entry defaults but not `id`, while the editor keys and selects entries by `e.id`.
detail.suggestion: Move parseSillyTavernLorebook out of LoreBookEditor.tsx into src/lib/lorebook.ts as `normaliseLoreBook(raw: unknown): LoreBook` (it is already self-contained), and call it at every entry point that produces a LoreBook — the editor's JSON drop, ImportPNG's onLoadLorebook call, DecodePNG's, and App.tsx's bridge openCard — so the `as LoreBook` casts disappear and there is one place where a foreign lorebook becomes the app's shape.

review::.::holistic::mid_level_elegance:.summary: Five parallel per-card-type callbacks repeated across App, Library, ImportPNG and DecodePNG, plus a dead pngData param

evidence: LibraryProps (Library.tsx lines 38-44) declares onEditCard/onEditLorebook/onEditScript/onEditScenario/onEditPersona; ImportPNGProps and DecodePNGProps each declare the same five as onLoad/onLoadLorebook/onLoadScript/onLoadScenario/onLoadPersona.

App.tsx carries four near-identical state pairs (lorebookKey/lorebookInit, scriptKey/scriptInit, scenarioKey/scenarioInit, personaKey/personaInit) and eight handlers (handleEditLorebook/Script/Scenario/Persona and handleImportLorebook/Script/Scenario/Persona) that differ only in which setter they call.
Library.handleEdit (line 127) and App's bridge openCard switch (line ~215) are two separate LibraryCard -> per-type-callback demultiplexers written independently.
onEditCard's second parameter is `pngData: Uint8Array | null` but App receives it as `_pngData` and ignores it; no caller of loadFromLibrary uses it.
detail.suggestion: Collapse the fan-out to one callback carrying a discriminated union: `type OpenRequest = { kind: "character"; card: TavernCardV2; imageSrc?: string; meta?: MetadataInfo; sourcePlatform?: PlatformId; libraryId?: string } | { kind: "lorebook"; book: LoreBook; imageSrc: string | null; libraryId?: string } | ...`, with `onOpen(req: OpenRequest)` replacing the five props in Library, ImportPNG and DecodePNG. In App, replace the four key/init pairs with a single `editorInit: OpenRequest | null` plus one `editorKey`, and drop the unused pngData parameter. That removes roughly 20 props and 8 handlers without adding an abstraction layer.

review::.::holistic::mid_level_elegance:.summary: Bridge persist() saves characters with pngData null and platform hardcoded, so an MCP update wipes both

evidence: client.ts persist() calls `saveCard(card, null, imageSrc, "sillytavern", existingId)` for every character write, including the update path where `existing` is already loaded.
library/index.ts saveCard builds a fresh LibraryCard and db.put()s it, preserving only createdAt — so pngData and platform are replaced by the values passed in.

CardPreviewPanel.tsx line 166 saves the encoded card PNG and the real target platform, and src/lib/archive/index.ts writes `cards/<name>.png` only `if (card.pngData)`. After any MCP update the archive silently degrades that card to JSON and its platform label reads "sillytavern".
detail.suggestion: In client.ts updateCard, pass the existing record's fields through: give persist() the existing LibraryCard (or explicit pngData and platform arguments) and call `saveCard(card, existing.pngData, existing.imageSrc, existing.platform, existing.id)` on the update path, keeping `null`/"sillytavern" only for creates.

review::.::holistic::mid_level_elegance:.summary: MCP create_script sends `code` but ScriptCard/ScriptEditor read `content`, so agent-created scripts arrive empty

evidence: mcp/src/index.ts create_script declares `code: z.string().describe("The script body.")` and spreads it straight into the card body via `create("script", { spec: "script_card_v1", ...data, ... })`.

src/types/index.ts ScriptCard declares `content: string`, and ScriptEditor.tsx line 121 renders `card.content`. Nothing between the MCP tool and the stored rawData renames the field, and the bridge's persist() for non-character types stores the body verbatim.
Every other create_* tool's field names line up with the target type, so this is a single divergence rather than a deliberate wire vocabulary.
detail.suggestion: Rename the input to `content` in create_script's inputSchema (keeping the same description), or map it explicitly at the tool boundary — `create("script", { spec: "script_card_v1", ...rest, content: code }, open)` — so the MCP tool and ScriptCard agree on one field name.

review::.::holistic::mid_level_elegance:.summary: Bridge invents findCard() over getAllCards() because the library module exposes no get-by-id

evidence: library/index.ts exports saveCard, saveAnyCard, getAllCards and deleteCard — no read-one, even though the IndexedDB store uses `id` as its keyPath.

client.ts findCard() does `(await getAllCards()).find((c) => c.id === id)`, and it is called on every cards.get, cards.update, cards.delete and app.open — each one deserialising every card in the library, pngData blobs and data-URL cover art included, to return one record.
detail.suggestion: Add `export async function getCard(id: string): Promise<LibraryCard | undefined>` to src/lib/library/index.ts using `(await getDb()).get(STORE, id)` with the same `cardType ?? "character"` normalisation getAllCards applies, and have client.ts findCard call it instead of scanning getAllCards.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::no_c.summary: No test environment configured, so all 30 components and 5 hooks are untestable, not just untested

evidence: vite.config.ts has no `test` block — no environment, no setupFiles, no coverage settings — and package.json devDependencies contain no jsdom/happy-dom and no @testing-library/*.
The suite consequently runs in Node, which is why all 4 test files sit under src/lib and target pure functions only.
The untested React surface is large and stateful: LoreBookEditor 585 LOC with 11 hooks, CardPreviewPanel 496, SmartImportPanel 432 with 11 useStates, Library 394, ScriptEditor 346.
detail.suggestion: Add a `test: { environment: 'jsdom' }` block to vite.config.ts and add jsdom plus @testing-library/react to devDependencies, then start with the two components carrying the most branching state — SmartImportPanel (sort-target routing and Quick Import) and LoreBookEditor (entry add/remove/reorder). This is setup that unblocks testing, not new abstraction.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::brid.summary: Security-critical HMAC handshake in bridge/protocol.ts is pure and node-testable but has zero tests

evidence: protocol.ts implements the mutual challenge-response the file's own comment says exists because 'loopback is not an authentication boundary': proveToken() HMAC-SHA256 hex and safeEqual() constant-time compare.

safeEqual returns early on a length mismatch and otherwise XOR-accumulates; proveToken pads each byte to two hex digits. Both are exactly the kind of code where a silent regression weakens the check rather than breaking it visibly.
Both functions are pure and depend only on crypto.subtle and TextEncoder, available in the Node 18 runtime the suite already uses — no environment work needed. Neither appears in any test file.
detail.suggestion: Add src/lib/bridge/protocol.test.ts asserting: proveToken is deterministic for a given (token, message) and differs when either changes; the hex output is 64 lowercase chars; safeEqual is true for identical strings and false for equal-length one-bit differences, differing lengths, and the empty string; and that a wrong token fails the app-side verification.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::mcp_.summary: The MCP server package shares the wire protocol with the app but has no tests and no test script

evidence: mcp/package.json defines no test script and mcp/src contains no test files.

protocol.ts states 'This file is imported by both sides. Keep it dependency-free' and carries BRIDGE_PROTOCOL_VERSION, bumped 'when the shape below changes incompatibly' — but nothing verifies the two sides agree on frame shapes, version, or close codes.
A protocol change therefore surfaces only as a runtime handshake failure between two separately built packages.
detail.suggestion: Add one handshake test that drives both halves against each other in-process: build a HelloFrame, produce the server's challenge proof with proveToken, verify it app-side, produce the auth proof, and assert the server accepts it — and assert it rejects a mismatched BRIDGE_PROTOCOL_VERSION with CLOSE_PROTOCOL. Adding a `test` script to mcp/package.json makes the server half runnable in CI.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::dete.summary: detectPlatform is an ordered heuristic chain on the import path with no tests, unlike its tested sibling detectCardShape

evidence: detectPlatform() branches in a fixed order — chara_card_v1/v2 with extensions.risuai/risu/chub, then agnai (kind+persona+sampleChat), janitorai (persona+greeting), backyard (aiName/basePrompt/initialMessage), venus (name+description+first_mes), else generic.
The later clauses overlap: a card with persona and greeting also usually has name and description, so reordering or adding a clause silently changes classification for real payloads.
detectCardShape, the other classifier on the same import path, has 9 tests including the misfiled-lorebook regression; detectPlatform has none.
detail.suggestion: Add cases to src/lib/platforms/converters.test.ts asserting detectPlatform returns the expected id for one representative payload per platform, including the discriminating ones: a chara_card_v2 with extensions.risuai -> 'risu', with extensions.chub -> 'chub', plain -> 'sillytavern', and a janitorai persona+greeting payload that also carries name+description still -> 'janitorai' (pinning clause order).

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::llm_.summary: The persona sorter's pure fallback layer over untrusted model output (coerceJson, budgetInput, sortPersonaAuto routing) has no tests

evidence: coerceJson tries three candidate shapes on raw model text (whole string, ```json fence contents, first-brace-to-last-brace slice) and returns null otherwise; its failure path is what raises "The model didn't return usable JSON" to the user.

budgetInput shrinks text by repeated 0.9 slicing until under the token limit, then walks back to a \n\n boundary only if it lies past the halfway point — an off-by-one here silently truncates a user's persona.
sortPersonaAuto decides between the deterministic parser and the model purely on heuristic.method ('labelled' | 'json' | 'wpp'), the routing rule the whole Quick Import UX rests on.
All three are module-private and untested, while the deterministic parser they fall back to has 26 tests.
detail.suggestion: Export coerceJson and budgetInput (or move them to a sibling module) and add a personaLlm test file covering: bare JSON, fenced JSON, JSON with prose before and after, an array response and a non-JSON response (both -> null); budgetInput leaving short text untouched and flagging truncated:true with a paragraph-boundary cut on long text; and sortPersonaAuto returning the parser result without touching the engine for labelled/json/wpp input.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::arch.summary: Archive filename-collision dedupe is a documented bug fix with no regression test, unlike comparable fixes elsewhere

evidence: exportCardsAsZip strips unsafe characters, falls back to card.id when the name sanitises to empty, and appends ' (n)' on collision, with a comment explaining that JSZip silently overwrites otherwise and 'an archive can never drop a card it claims to contain'.
The manifest entry must use the same disambiguated filename as the zip entry or the manifest points at a file that is not there — an invariant nothing checks.
Every other documented regression of this kind in the repo (JanitorAI placeholder round trip, generic character_version, negative PNG chunk length) has a test pinning it; this one does not.
detail.suggestion: Extract the name-disambiguation loop into an exported helper (e.g. uniqueArchiveName(name, id, used)) and test it directly: two cards named 'Rook' produce 'Rook' and 'Rook (2)'; a name of only punctuation falls back to the card id; and the manifest `file` value equals the key actually written to the zip.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: saveCard and saveAnyCard take incompatible positional parameter lists for the same 'persist a card' job

evidence: saveCard(cardData: TavernCardV2, pngData, imageSrc, platform, existingId?) vs saveAnyCard(cardType, name, rawData, imageSrc, tags, existingId?) — only imageSrc and existingId occupy comparable positions, and saveAnyCard is six positional params.
tags is derived from cardData.data.tags inside saveCard but must be supplied positionally to saveAnyCard; platform is a caller argument in one and hardcoded to cardType in the other.

src/lib/bridge/client.ts defines a private persist(cardType, body, imageSrc, existingId) whose entire body is an if/else picking between the two and shuffling arguments — the adapter exists only because the two signatures disagree.
detail.suggestion: Collapse both into one exported saveLibraryCard(input: { cardType, name?, cardData?, rawData?, pngData?, imageSrc, platform?, tags?, existingId? }): Promise<LibraryCard>, deriving name/tags from cardData when cardType is 'character'. Update the ~6 call sites (bridge/client.ts, CardPreviewPanel, LoreBookEditor, PersonaEditor, ScenarioEditor, ScriptEditor) and delete persist() from bridge/client.ts — this removes a function rather than adding one.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: SortOptions.signal is ignored on the WebLLM backend and onProgress is ignored on the endpoint backend

evidence: SortOptions declares { settings?, target?, onProgress?, signal? } as one public options bag on sortPersonaWithAi and sortPersonaAuto.
sortPersonaWithAi routes opts.signal only into runEndpoint(input, settings, target, opts.signal) and opts.onProgress only into runWebLlm(input, settings, target, opts.onProgress).

settings.backend defaults to 'webllm' (src/lib/personaLlm/settings.ts DEFAULTS), so a caller passing an AbortSignal on the default path gets no cancellation and no error — the model download and inference run to completion.
No caller in src/ passes signal at all today (only SmartImportPanel.tsx calls these functions, via runSort), so the option is advertised and untested.
detail.suggestion: Either honour signal on the WebLLM path (check signal.aborted before getEngine and after the completion resolves, throwing a DOMException 'AbortError'), or split the two backends' capabilities in the type — e.g. document on SortOptions that `signal` applies to the endpoint backend only and `onProgress` to the WebLLM backend only, with a one-line JSDoc on each field. The doc-only fix is the smaller change if cancellation is not actually needed.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: Three localStorage-backed settings modules each chose a different read verb, write contract, and return type

evidence: saveSettings(settings: AppSettings): void replaces wholesale and returns nothing (src/lib/settings.ts).
saveSorterSettings(patch: Partial<SorterSettings>): SorterSettings merges over current, notifies subscribers, and returns the merged value (src/lib/personaLlm/settings.ts).
setBridgeToken(token: string) is a bare setter with no return and no notification (src/lib/bridge/client.ts:47).
Read verbs drift across the same concern: loadStoredSettings(), getSorterSettings(), getBridgeToken(), getCustomTemplates().
detail.suggestion: Pick one contract for persisted settings and apply it to all three: `getX(): X` for reads and `saveX(patch: Partial<X>): X` for writes (the sorter's shape, which is the most useful of the three). Rename loadStoredSettings to getAppSettings and change saveSettings to take a partial and return the merged value; leave setBridgeToken alone if the token stays a single scalar, or fold it into the same shape.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: validateTavernCardV2 and validateJson in the same module return differently shaped results

evidence: validateTavernCardV2(card): ValidationResult — { valid, errors: string[], warnings: string[] }.
validateJson(jsonStr): { valid: boolean; error?: string } — inline anonymous type, singular `error`, no warnings.
Both are exported from src/lib/validators/index.ts with the same verb prefix, so a caller must remember which one uses `errors` and which uses `error`.
detail.suggestion: Have validateJson return ValidationResult too: `return { valid: false, errors: [(e as Error).message], warnings: [] }`. Update its call sites to read `.errors[0]`. This deletes the inline type rather than adding one.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: create_lorebook omits the shared tags field and update_card re-declares `open` without openAfter's data-loss warning

evidence: mcp/src/index.ts defines shared zod shapes `tags` and `openAfter` and uses them in create_character, create_persona, create_scenario, create_script.

create_lorebook's inputSchema has no `tags` entry, so a lorebook created through MCP can never carry tags — even though CardSummary.tags, saveAnyCard's tags parameter, and list_cards all support tags for lorebooks.

update_card declares `open: z.boolean().optional().describe("Bring the card up in the editor afterwards.")` instead of reusing openAfter, dropping the sentence 'opening a card replaces whatever the user is currently editing, and any unsaved work in that panel is lost' — the one tool most likely to be called mid-edit is the one that no longer warns.
create_character uses `character_version` while the other four create_* tools use `version`; this one is defensible (Tavern v2 spec) but is undocumented as deliberate.
detail.suggestion: Add `tags,` to create_lorebook's inputSchema and pass it through to create(); replace update_card's inline `open` declaration with the shared `openAfter` constant. Both are one-line edits in mcp/src/index.ts.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: convertTo* returns two different types across the same family, forcing four double-casts in the dispatcher

evidence: convertToSillyTavern, convertToChub, convertToRisu return TavernCardV2; convertToJanitorAI, convertToAgnai, convertToVenus, convertToBackyard, convertToGeneric return Record<string, unknown>.

convertCardTo therefore writes `as unknown as Record<string, unknown>` on the sillytavern, chub and risu arms — a double cast that defeats the type check at the exact point the family is supposed to be uniform.

The inverse family is asymmetric too: convertFrom* exists only for janitorai, agnai and backyard; the other five are handled by inline code in convertCardFrom's default branch, so a developer adding a platform cannot tell from the export list which half of the pattern to follow.
detail.suggestion: Declare every convertTo* as returning Record<string, unknown> (TavernCardV2 already structurally satisfies it for the three that return clones), removing all four `as unknown as` casts from convertCardTo. Leave convertFrom*'s default-branch handling as is, but add a one-line comment above convertCardFrom's default naming the five platforms it covers so the asymmetry reads as deliberate.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: getCarrierPng's docstring promises it never throws for unsupported formats, but it rejects for any undecodable data:image/*

evidence: The docstring reads 'PNG bytes for the given cover image ... Never throws for a merely-unsupported format.'

getCarrierPng falls back to MINIMAL_PNG only for a falsy imageSrc or a src that does not start with 'data:image/'. Anything matching 'data:image/' (e.g. data:image/tiff) is passed to imageSrcToPngBytes, whose img.onerror handler rejects with 'Could not read the image'.
Callers in CardPreviewPanel.tsx (two sites), LoreBookEditor.tsx and PersonaEditor.tsx all wrap it in try/catch, so the stated contract is what is wrong, not the behaviour at the call sites.
detail.suggestion: Make the code match the doc: wrap the imageSrcToPngBytes branch in try/catch and return MINIMAL_PNG on failure, or reword the docstring to 'Falls back to a 1x1 PNG when there is no image; rejects if a data:image/* URL cannot be decoded.' The reword is the smaller change and preserves the current caller error messages.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: personaParser exports CardField and its alias PersonaField and uses both in public signatures; header doc names exports that don't exist

evidence: `export type PersonaField = CardField;` is documented as a 'Historical alias', yet both names remain in public signatures: ParsedPersona.fields is Partial<Record<PersonaField, string>> while toCharacterFields returns Partial<Record<CardField, string>>.
src/components/PersonaEditor.tsx imports PersonaField while the parser's own label/order constants are typed on CardField, so a reader has to confirm the two are the same type.

The module header comment says 'See PERSONA_FIELDS and CHARACTER_FIELDS' — neither export exists; the actual exports are PERSONA_FIELD_LABELS / PERSONA_FIELD_ORDER and CHARACTER_FIELD_LABELS / CHARACTER_FIELD_ORDER.
detail.suggestion: Switch ParsedPersona.fields to Partial<Record<CardField, string>> and PersonaEditor.tsx's import to CardField, then delete the PersonaField alias. Fix the header comment to name PERSONA_FIELD_ORDER and CHARACTER_FIELD_ORDER. Both are net deletions.

review::.::holistic::authorization_consi.summary: Authenticated bridge peer can delete/overwrite any card with no confirmation and no audit record, unlike every UI path

evidence: src/lib/bridge/client.ts handle() dispatches cards.delete and cards.update straight to deleteCard/persist; the only trace left is setState({ served, lastMethod }) held in memory for the status light.

Every UI destructive path gates on ConfirmModal first — Library.tsx confirmDelete ('Deletes are irreversible and there is no undo, so both paths confirm first'), Templates.tsx, App.tsx clear-card — so the same invariant is enforced for the human and skipped for the agent.
The only mitigation on the agent path is prose in the tool description in mcp/src/index.ts ('There is no undo — confirm with the user first'), which the model may ignore.
detail.suggestion: Give the bridge the same confirmation the UI enforces for the same operations: route cards.delete (and cards.update when it overwrites an existing card) through the existing ConfirmModal via a host hook, so the promise resolves only after the user approves, and append a bounded in-app log of served methods with card id and timestamp instead of only a counter. Reuse ConfirmModal and the registerBridgeHost callback that already exists rather than adding a new permission layer.

review::.::holistic::authorization_consi.summary: Sibling bridge handlers disagree on validating peer input: create checks cardType/imageSrc, update merges any patch unchecked

evidence: createCard validates params.cardType against ALLOWED_CARD_TYPES and runs safeImageSrc, which rejects non-data: image URLs with an explicit beacon rationale.

updateCard does no validation at all: `const merged = { ...(bodyOf(existing) ?? {}), ...(params.patch ?? {}) }` writes every key and type the peer sends; handle() casts all params with `as` (`req.params as UpdateParams`) so nothing else checks them either.
A patch like { tags: "solo" } persists a string where an array is assumed, and Library.tsx:72 `c.tags.some(...)` and :362 `card.tags.length` read it directly on the next render.
detail.suggestion: Validate patch at the same place create is validated: in updateCard, drop or coerce keys whose type disagrees with the existing card body (at minimum enforce tags as string[] and reject non-string scalars for text fields), and re-run safeImageSrc if a patch is ever allowed to carry imageSrc. Keep it as inline checks in client.ts next to safeImageSrc rather than introducing a schema layer.

review::.::holistic::ai_generated_debt::.summary: exportPng/handleSaveToLibrary/clearForNew copied verbatim across four editor components

evidence: ScenarioEditor.tsx:66-74, ScriptEditor.tsx:65-74, PersonaEditor.tsx:75-84 and LoreBookEditor.tsx:208-217 contain byte-identical exportPng() bodies apart from the card-type string passed to encodeCharaToPng.

handleSaveToLibrary() is likewise identical at ScenarioEditor.tsx:76-88, ScriptEditor.tsx:76-88, PersonaEditor.tsx:86-98 and LoreBookEditor.tsx:219-232 — same setSaving dance, same `versionChanged` computation, same three-way success ternary, same bare `catch { setMsg("Failed to save to library.", false); }`.

The same four files each repeat clearForNew(), a Partial-patch update(), the same five useState declarations, and an identical `// Auto-sync filename to <type> name` useEffect (LoreBookEditor.tsx:110, PersonaEditor.tsx:46, ScenarioEditor.tsx:45, ScriptEditor.tsx:42).
detail.suggestion: Extract one hook, e.g. `useCardEditorIO(cardType, { card, imageSrc, fileSuffix })` in src/hooks/, returning `{ outputFileName, setOutputFileName, saving, libraryId, exportJson, exportPng, saveToLibrary, clearForNew, status, setMsg }`. Each of the four editors then calls it once and keeps only its own field JSX. This is a net reduction — one implementation replaces four copies and one new file replaces roughly 200 duplicated lines — and it removes the risk that a fix to the save path lands in three editors out of four.

review::.::holistic::ai_generated_debt::.summary: App.tsx repeats eight mechanically identical editor-open handlers over four parallel state pairs

evidence: src/App.tsx:167-190 defines handleEditLorebook/handleEditScript/handleEditScenario/handleEditPersona, each a three-line body that sets `<type>Init`, bumps `<type>Key`, and calls setActivePage — differing only in which state setters they name.
src/App.tsx:192-212 then repeats all four as handleImportLorebook/Script/Scenario/Persona, whose only difference from the Edit variants is that the init object omits `id`.
Backing them are four parallel `<type>Init` / `<type>Key` useState pairs (App.tsx:47-70), which is a large share of why the file carries 15 useStates.
detail.suggestion: Collapse the four Init/Key pairs into one `editorInit` state of the shape `{ type: NonCharCardType; card: unknown; imageSrc: string | null; id?: string }` plus a single `editorKey`, and replace the eight handlers with one `openEditor(type, card, imageSrc, id?)`. Callers pass the type they already know; the four Init props feeding the editors become one lookup on `editorInit.type`. That deletes eight state variables and seven handlers without adding an abstraction layer.

review::.::holistic::ai_generated_debt::.summary: Identical PNG-bytes-to-data-URL helper copy-pasted into two components

evidence: src/components/DecodePNG.tsx:54-58 declares uint8ToDataUrl inside the processFile useCallback: a char-by-char accumulation loop followed by `return "data:image/png;base64," + btoa(bin);`.
src/components/ImportPNG.tsx:37-39 contains the same loop and the same return expression at module scope.
The inverse conversion already lives in a lib module (base64ToBytes in src/lib/carrierImage.ts:33-38), so the codebase's own convention puts this helper in src/lib/.
detail.suggestion: Move it to src/lib/carrierImage.ts as `export function pngBytesToDataUrl(bytes: Uint8Array): string` next to the existing base64ToBytes, and import it in both components. One exported function replaces two inline copies — no new file, no new layer.

review::.::holistic::ai_generated_debt::.summary: getCardTokenBreakdown restates the same nine field names three times over

evidence: src/lib/tokenizer/index.ts:26-57 declares nine `const <field> = countTokens(d.<field>)` locals, then lists all nine again as object properties, then adds all nine again by hand to compute `total`.
Adding a tenth counted field means editing three places, and forgetting the third leaves `total` silently wrong — the kind of drift the shape invites rather than prevents.
detail.suggestion: Keep the CardTokenBreakdown interface, but build the counts by iterating a `const COUNTED_FIELDS = ["description", "personality", ...] as const` list into an object and computing `total` with a reduce over its values; alternate_greetings stays its own line since it sums an array. Shorter than the current body and makes the total impossible to desynchronise.

review::.::holistic::incomplete_migratio.summary: Shape-based card routing adopted by ImportPNG only; DecodePNG keeps a duplicate constant and the old keyword-trusting path

evidence: src/lib/cardShape.ts's header documents the bug it exists to fix: the importer trusted the PNG metadata keyword, so a lorebook exported under the 'chara' key was rebuilt as a blank character card and every entry was silently dropped behind a success message.
src/components/ImportPNG.tsx:8,90-92 imports shapeForKey/detectCardShape, reconciles claimed vs actual shape, and even surfaces a mismatch note to the user.

src/components/DecodePNG.tsx:11 redeclares `const CHARACTER_KEYS = new Set(["chara", "character", "tavern", "tavern_card_v2"])` — byte-identical to the CHARACTER_KEYS exported from src/lib/cardShape.ts:16 — and never imports cardShape at all.

DecodePNG's handleLoadToEditor (lines 106-120) dispatches solely on result.key: `if (CHARACTER_KEYS.has(result.key) && result.sourcePlatform)` then convertCardFrom, else literal comparisons against "lorebook"/"script"/"scenario"/"persona". The same mislabelled file that ImportPNG now handles correctly is still silently emptied here.
src/components/ImportPNG.tsx:36 and src/components/DecodePNG.tsx:54 additionally each hold their own uint8ToDataUrl copy.
detail.suggestion: Delete the local CHARACTER_KEYS at src/components/DecodePNG.tsx:11 and import { shapeForKey, detectCardShape } from '../lib/cardShape'. In processFile compute `const effective = detectCardShape(parsed) ?? shapeForKey(key)` and store that on result alongside key; in handleLoadToEditor and the isCharCard flag dispatch on the stored shape instead of result.key. That removes a duplicated constant and a whole routing policy rather than adding anything.

review::.::holistic::incomplete_migratio.summary: detectCardShape accepts chara_card_v3 but the type, validator and converters are v2-only, so v3 cards import as blank

evidence: src/lib/cardShape.ts:45: `if (spec === "chara_card_v2" || spec === "chara_card_v3") return "character";` — the only mention of v3 in the repository.

src/types/index.ts:45 declares `spec: "chara_card_v2"` and src/lib/validators/index.ts:36 pushes "Invalid spec — expected 'chara_card_v2'" for anything else, so v3 blocks export whenever autoValidateBeforeExport is on.

src/lib/platforms/converters.ts:200 gates the normalising branch on `obj.spec === "chara_card_v2"`; a v3 card misses it and falls into the fallback that reads top-level obj.description/obj.personality/obj.scenario. A v3 card nests those under `data`, so ImportPNG (line 117) reports 'Loaded character ... Opening in editor…' while handing the editor an empty card — the same silent-data-loss shape cardShape.ts was created to eliminate.
detail.suggestion: Pick one end of the half-step. Either drop `|| spec === "chara_card_v3"` from src/lib/cardShape.ts:45 so v3 files are reported as unrecognised instead of silently emptied, or widen the single gate in src/lib/platforms/converters.ts:200 to `obj.spec === "chara_card_v2" || obj.spec === "chara_card_v3"` (v3's data block is a v2 superset, so the existing spread-onto-blank normalisation already handles it) and relax the spec check in validators to accept both. The first option is one deletion and is the simpler fix if v3 is not actually a goal.

review::.::holistic::incomplete_migratio.summary: cardType legacy fallback re-applied at five call sites downstream of the function that already normalises it, and omitted at others

evidence: src/lib/library/index.ts:89-94 getAllCards() is the single read path out of IndexedDB and maps `cardType: c.cardType ?? "character"` over every record, as its docstring states.

Every LibraryCard in src/components/Library.tsx comes from that call (line 58), yet lines 71, 84, 128 and 286 each re-apply `(c.cardType ?? "character")`; src/lib/archive/index.ts:31 does the same on cards handed to it from that list.
src/App.tsx:224 (`switch (card.cardType)`) and src/lib/bridge/client.ts:281/291/297 read the same field with no fallback, so the two conventions sit side by side.
LibraryCard.cardType is declared non-optional in src/types/index.ts:181, so the `??` arms are unreachable under the type and a reader cannot tell whether undefined is genuinely possible.
detail.suggestion: Delete the `?? "character"` fallbacks at src/components/Library.tsx:71, 84, 128, 286 and src/lib/archive/index.ts:31, leaving getAllCards() as the single normalisation point named in its docstring. Five deletions, no new code.

review::.::holistic::package_organizatio.summary: src/components/ is 29 flat files mixing routed pages, single-parent children and shared primitives

evidence: 29 .tsx files, 5592 LOC, zero subdirectories; directory_profiles reports avg_fan_in 1.7 across them.

Measured fan-in splits them into three groups with different ownership: 13 files imported only by App.tsx (routed pages), 8 files with exactly one importer (CardPreviewPanel, CharacterEditor, JSONView, RawPreview <- CreateCard; PlatformSelector <- CardPreviewPanel; SorterSettings <- SmartImportPanel; BridgeStatusLight, LlmStatusLight <- Sidebar), and 6 files with fan-in 2-5 that are true shared primitives (TagInput 5, ResizableTextArea 5, ConfirmClearPanel 4, ImageDropzone 4, TextAreaField 3, ConfirmModal 2).

Nothing in the filename encodes which group a file is in: the 'Panel' suffix covers a 496-LOC feature child (CardPreviewPanel), a 432-LOC feature child (SmartImportPanel) and a 48-LOC shared primitive (ConfirmClearPanel).
Consequence: a developer editing CardPreviewPanel.tsx cannot tell from the tree that only CreateCard renders it, and editing ConfirmClearPanel.tsx gives no signal that four editors depend on it.
detail.suggestion: Split by measured fan-in into three purpose-named folders, no new abstraction and no barrel files. Stage 1 (shared, lowest risk): create src/components/ui/ and git mv TagInput.tsx ResizableTextArea.tsx TextAreaField.tsx ImageDropzone.tsx ConfirmModal.tsx ConfirmClearPanel.tsx JSONView.tsx RawPreview.tsx into it. Stage 2: create src/components/pages/ and move the 13 App-mounted views (CreateCard, ImportPNG, DecodePNG, Templates, Settings, HelpAbout, Library, LoreBookEditor, ScriptEditor, ScenarioEditor, PersonaEditor, Sidebar, ErrorBoundary). Stage 3: leave the remaining single-parent children beside their parent page or under src/components/editor/ (CardPreviewPanel, CharacterEditor, PlatformSelector, FieldCompatibility, SmartImportPanel, SorterSettings, BridgeStatusLight, LlmStatusLight). After each stage run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build`; relative import paths are the only thing to fix and tsc lists every one.

review::.::holistic::package_organizatio.summary: mcp/ package reaches into src/lib via ../../ for four node-safe modules that look like their browser-only siblings

evidence: mcp/ has its own package.json, node_modules and dependency set, yet mcp/src/bridge.ts line 13 imports ../../src/lib/bridge/protocol.js and mcp/src/index.ts lines 24-27 import ../../src/lib/validators/index.js, ../../src/lib/platforms/index.js and ../../src/lib/personaParser/index.js.
mcp/tsconfig.json needs "rootDir": ".." purely to make those escapes compile.

The four shared modules are DOM-free while their siblings under src/lib/ are not (library/ -> idb, archive/ -> jszip, carrierImage.ts -> canvas, customTemplates/ -> localStorage), so nothing in the directory layout warns that editing src/lib/platforms/index.ts changes the MCP server's behaviour.

This has already drifted: mcp/tsconfig.json's "include" array lists ../src/lib/bridge/protocol.ts and ../src/lib/personaParser/index.ts only — validators/index.ts and platforms/index.ts are imported but not declared.
detail.suggestion: Make the boundary visible with a move, not a build-system change. Create src/shared/ and git mv src/lib/bridge/protocol.ts, src/lib/validators/, src/lib/platforms/ and src/lib/personaParser/ under it, leaving browser-only code in src/lib/. Order: move personaParser and validators first (each has one non-mcp importer group), then platforms, then protocol.ts (update src/lib/bridge/client.ts alongside). Then update mcp/tsconfig.json's include to ../src/shared/**/*.ts — one glob that cannot go stale, replacing the hand-maintained two-entry list. Validate with `npx tsc --noEmit` at the repo root, `npm --prefix mcp run typecheck`, `npm --prefix mcp run build` and `npm test`.

review::.::holistic::package_organizatio.summary: src/data/templates/ronalVoss.ts is a two-deep folder for one file whose name hides the template catalog it holds

evidence: src/data/ and src/data/templates/ each contain exactly one entry, terminating in a single 76-line file.
The file's name identifies one sample character, but it exports the whole built-in catalog: ronanVossTemplate (line 3), blankTemplate (line 42) and templates (line 63).

Both importers want the catalog, not the sample: App.tsx line 7 imports blankTemplate — the empty card every new project starts from — and Templates.tsx line 4 imports templates. A developer looking for the app's blank-card default would not search a file named after a character.

detail.suggestion: git mv src/data/templates/ronalVoss.ts src/data/builtinTemplates.ts and delete the now-empty src/data/templates/ directory, then fix the two import paths in src/App.tsx (line 7) and src/components/Templates.tsx (line 4). This is a rename plus two edits and removes a directory level rather than adding one. Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build`.

review::.::holistic::initialization_coup.summary: Bridge host must be registered before initBridge(), enforced only by statement order; wrong order fails silently

evidence: src/lib/bridge/client.ts:90 declares `let host: BridgeHost | null = null`, populated only by the exported `registerBridgeHost()` at line 92.
`initBridge()` (line 123) opens the socket and can begin serving RPCs immediately; there is no assertion, warning, or queueing that `host` was set first.

Every consumer optional-chains: `host?.onLibraryChanged?.()` and `host?.openCard(saved)` at lines 358, 359, 372, 373, 386. An `app.open` RPC arriving before registration therefore resolves successfully to the MCP server while doing nothing in the UI — the agent is told the card was opened when it was not.

The ordering is correct today only because src/App.tsx:219-243 puts registerBridgeHost and initBridge in that order inside one useEffect. That effect also has no cleanup, so the registration and the socket outlive an App unmount.
detail.suggestion: Fold registration into the entry point so ordering is structural rather than conventional: change the signature to `export function initBridge(h: BridgeHost)` which sets `host = h` before calling `open()`, and delete the separate `registerBridgeHost` export. App.tsx then makes one call instead of two, and it becomes impossible to start the bridge without a host. This removes an exported function and a call site rather than adding anything.

review::.::holistic::initialization_coup.summary: initBridge() calls open() without honouring the manualDisconnect latch, so a re-entry can strand status at "connecting"

evidence: `scheduleReconnect()` (line 128) begins `if (manualDisconnect || reconnectTimer) return;` — the latch is the module's stated way to stop retrying after a deliberate refusal (bad token at line 186, rejected pairing at line 207, close codes at lines 236/241).
`initBridge()` (line 123) is `if (isBridgeEnabled()) open();` — it consults the persisted ENABLED_KEY but not the in-memory latch, and unlike `connectBridge()` (line 108) it does not reset it either.

If initBridge runs while manualDisconnect is true, `open()` sets status "connecting" at line 140, then `onclose` hits `if (manualDisconnect) return;` at line 232 and never reports anything — the MCP light stays on "connecting" indefinitely with no error text.
Unreachable today only by accident: App.tsx's effect deps are all `useCallback(..., [])` so the effect runs once, but nothing in client.ts documents or defends that assumption.
detail.suggestion: Make initBridge respect the same latch as the reconnect path: `export function initBridge() { if (isBridgeEnabled() && !manualDisconnect) open(); }`. One line, and it makes the two paths into open() agree on when a deliberate refusal means stop.

review::.::holistic::initialization_coup.summary: One consumer subscribes to the sorter-settings store, the other samples it — correct only while there is a single writer

evidence: src/lib/personaLlm/settings.ts:37-56 maintains a module-level listener set and notifies on every `saveSorterSettings`, with a docstring recording the bug that motivated it (a stale copy in the sidebar light could start a multi-gigabyte download of a deselected model).
src/components/LlmStatusLight.tsx:22 honours that contract: `useEffect(() => subscribeSorterSettings(setSettings), [])`.

src/components/SmartImportPanel.tsx:68 does not: it seeds `useState<Settings>(() => getSorterSettings())` and thereafter only updates from its own `setSettings(saveSorterSettings(patch))` at line 114. It holds a private snapshot of shared module state with no subscription.

This is safe only because SmartImportPanel is currently the sole writer in the codebase — a second writer (a settings screen, or a bridge RPC) would leave it silently stale, which is exactly the failure the listener set was added to prevent.
detail.suggestion: Give SmartImportPanel the same one-line subscription as LlmStatusLight: `useEffect(() => subscribeSorterSettings(setSettings), []);` next to its existing state. `saveSorterSettings` already notifies and returns the merged value, so line 114 can stay as-is; the subscription just closes the hole for any future writer. Alternatively, if the store gains more consumers, replace both local snapshots with a `useSorterSettings()` hook built on useSyncExternalStore, matching how useEngineState and useBridgeState already consume the sibling stores.

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::d.summary: Four card editors restate the same shell — state, filename effect, save/export handlers and export aside — differing only by kind literal

evidence: Diffing ScenarioEditor.tsx:30-95 against ScriptEditor.tsx:30-88 yields only the card type parameter and the string 'scenario' vs 'script': identical card/imageSrc/status/libraryId/saving/savedVersion/outputFileName state, identical filename-sync useEffect, identical update(), clearForNew(), exportJson(), exportPng(), and handleSaveToLibrary() including the versionChanged branch and the three-way success message.
PersonaEditor.tsx:35-95 is the same block again with 'persona'; LoreBookEditor.tsx:94-220 is the same block with a lorebook-specific buildExportData.

The export <aside> repeats too: ScenarioEditor.tsx:140-212 and LoreBookEditor.tsx's aside share the same Output Settings / metadata key / version / Save-or-Update / Export JSON / Embed in PNG / status-paragraph / footer-blurb structure verbatim.
Consequence: the version-bump-forks-a-new-record rule and the save/export error handling exist in four places and must be changed in four places.
detail.suggestion: Extract the shared state and handlers into one hook, e.g. src/hooks/useCardEditor.ts taking (kind, defaultCard, initialCard, initialImageSrc, initialLibraryId) and returning { card, update, imageSrc, setImageSrc, outputFileName, setOutputFileName, libraryId, saving, status, clearForNew, exportJson, exportPng, saveToLibrary } — with the kind string driving the filename suffix, the PNG metadata key and the 'Unnamed X' fallback. Pair it with one <CardExportPanel kind=... /> for the duplicated aside. LoreBookEditor passes its buildExportData as the serializer; the other three pass the card itself. This removes roughly 400 lines net and leaves one place to change save semantics.

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::s.summary: ScenarioEditor is a copy of the shared editor shell; its only original content is the field layout and token readout

evidence: ScenarioEditor.tsx:34-90 (state block, filename effect, update, clearForNew, exportJson, exportPng, handleSaveToLibrary) is character-for-character the same as ScriptEditor.tsx:31-84 apart from the ScenarioCard type and the 'scenario' literal.
The 216-LOC file's genuinely scenario-specific content is the field grid (lines 105-135) and the two-field token readout (lines 145-155).

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::p.summary: PersonaEditor repeats the same editor shell; its only unique logic is applySmartImport and the isBlank check

evidence: PersonaEditor.tsx:35-95 duplicates the state block, filename-sync effect, update, clearForNew, exportJson, exportPng and handleSaveToLibrary found in ScenarioEditor and ScriptEditor, differing only in the PersonaCard type and the 'persona' literal.
