review::.::holistic::design_coherence::p.summary: Four identically-shaped per-type callbacks are threaded through five components instead of one onOpenCard(type, ...)

evidence: App.tsx:159-200 declares handleEditLorebook/handleEditScript/handleEditScenario/handleEditPersona and handleImportLorebook/Script/Scenario/Persona — eight useCallbacks whose bodies differ only in which of the four (key, init) state pairs they set and which page they navigate to.
App.tsx also keeps four parallel state pairs (lorebookKey/lorebookInit, scriptKey/scriptInit, scenarioKey/scenarioInit, personaKey/personaInit) declared at lines 51-68 with identical shapes.

The same four callbacks are then redeclared as props in ImportPNG.tsx:14-17, DecodePNG.tsx:23-26 and Library.tsx:41-44 — all four with the identical signature (data, imageSrc, id?) => void — and re-branched over in ImportPNG.tsx:122-160, DecodePNG.tsx:116-119 and Library.tsx:128-139.
A fifth branch over the same five types sits in App.tsx's registerBridgeHost openCard switch (lines 210-230).
detail.suggestion: Collapse the four callbacks into one prop, onOpenCard(type: LibraryCardType, data: unknown, imageSrc: string | null, libraryId?: string), and hold a single editor slot in App: const [editorInit, setEditorInit] = useState<{type, data, imageSrc, id?}>() with one key counter. Library.tsx already has TYPE_ORDER/SECTION_META and DecodePNG already has NON_CHAR_META — the branch chains become a lookup against those. This deletes six of the eight App handlers and three four-line if-chains, and makes adding a card type a one-line table entry.

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::d.summary: DecodePNG re-branches over the five card types with four optional callbacks despite already owning a type table

evidence: DecodePNG.tsx:14-19 defines NON_CHAR_META, a Record<NonCharType, {label, icon, color}> that already enumerates lorebook/script/scenario/persona and is used for the detection badge.
handleLoadToEditor (lines 110-120) nevertheless dispatches through four separate optional props with a hand-written if-chain — the same four keys the table already lists.
The four props are optional (onLoadLorebook?, onLoadScript?, ...) yet App.tsx always supplies all four, so the optionality only hides a silently-does-nothing path if one is ever omitted.
detail.suggestion: Replace the four optional props with a single required onOpenCard(type, data, imageSrc) and drive handleLoadToEditor off the existing NON_CHAR_META keys, keeping only the character branch (which needs convertCardFrom and the meta object) separate.

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::l.summary: SillyTavern lorebook parsing and serialization live inside LoreBookEditor while all other format logic lives in src/lib

evidence: parseSillyTavernLorebook (LoreBookEditor.tsx:47-84) handles the entries-as-object-or-array variance and the name/comment aliasing — pure format knowledge with no React in it.
buildExportData (lines 165-193) is the matching serializer, reindexing entries and emitting the ST field order.

Every comparable concern is a lib module: src/lib/platforms/converters.ts, src/lib/pngMetadata, src/lib/personaParser, src/lib/validators. The MCP server imports those directly (mcp/src/index.ts:24-26) precisely so there is one implementation of each rule; the lorebook rules are not importable that way.

mcp/src/index.ts's create_lorebook tool therefore re-states the entry defaults (secondary_keys, enabled, constant, selective, case_sensitive, insertion_order, priority) that DEFAULT_ENTRY in LoreBookEditor.tsx:20-34 already defines.
detail.suggestion: Move parseSillyTavernLorebook, buildExportData and DEFAULT_ENTRY into a new src/lib/lorebook/index.ts and import them from both LoreBookEditor.tsx and mcp/src/index.ts, matching how converters/validators/personaParser are already shared. The component keeps only state and rendering.

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::d.summary: blankTemplate literal duplicates createBlankTavernCard() exactly — two definitions of the empty spec-valid card

evidence: src/data/templates/ronalVoss.ts:42-61 spells out spec, spec_version and all fifteen data keys.
src/lib/tavernCard.ts:4-24 produces the identical object from createBlankTavernCard(), documented as 'the starting shape for every import path'.

App.tsx imports blankTemplate for both its initial project and clearCard, while src/lib/bridge/client.ts's persist() uses createBlankTavernCard — so a new spec field has to be added in two places or the two paths silently diverge.
detail.suggestion: Replace the literal with `export const blankTemplate: TavernCardV2 = createBlankTavernCard();` in ronalVoss.ts (importing from ../../lib/tavernCard), leaving one definition of the empty card.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: MCP update_card promises 'everything else is left alone' but wipes pngData and resets platform to sillytavern

evidence: mcp/src/index.ts update_card description: 'Shallow-merge changes into a card already in the library. Only the fields you pass are touched; everything else is left alone.'

src/lib/bridge/client.ts persist() for cardType 'character' calls saveCard(card, null, imageSrc, "sillytavern", existingId) — the pngData argument is hardcoded null and platform is hardcoded 'sillytavern'.

src/lib/archive/index.ts:19 exports a card as PNG only when card.pngData is set, so a bridge-updated card silently downgrades to JSON in the next archive; src/components/Library.tsx:292 shows card.platform as the card's badge.
detail.suggestion: Have persist() take the existing LibraryCard when one is being updated and carry its pngData and platform through instead of hardcoding null/'sillytavern' — updateCard already loads the record via findCard(params.id), so pass `existing.pngData` and `existing.platform` into saveCard. Alternatively, if dropping the PNG is intended, say so in the update_card description.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: MCP create_script writes `code`, but ScriptCard and ScriptEditor read `content`, so agent-created scripts open empty

evidence: mcp/src/index.ts create_script inputSchema declares `code: z.string().describe("The script body.")` and spreads it straight into the card body.
src/types/index.ts ScriptCard declares `content: string`; src/components/ScriptEditor.tsx:121 renders `<CodeEditor value={card.content} …>`, which is undefined for a bridge-created script.
src/lib/cardShape.ts detectCardShape identifies a script by `typeof obj.content === "string"`, so the same payload is also unrecognisable on re-import.
detail.suggestion: Rename the create_script input field from `code` to `content` (keeping the description), or map it in the handler: `create("script", { spec: "script_card_v1", ...rest, content: code, version: version ?? "1.0" }, open)`.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: validateTavernCardV2 declares TavernCardV2 but is written for untrusted input, so every caller casts past the signature

evidence: src/lib/validators/index.ts:32 signature is `validateTavernCardV2(card: TavernCardV2)`, yet the body checks `!card || typeof card !== "object"`, treats `card.data` as possibly undefined, and reports errors like "'tags' must be an array, got string" — none of which the declared type permits.
mcp/src/index.ts:328 calls it as `validateTavernCardV2({ ... } as never)`; src/lib/platforms/converters.test.ts:148 uses the same `as never` escape.
detail.suggestion: Change the parameter to `card: unknown` and narrow internally (the guards already exist), then delete the `as never` at mcp/src/index.ts:328 and in converters.test.ts. This removes two casts rather than adding anything.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: LibraryCard.rawData is `unknown` but cast straight to LoreBook/ScriptCard/ScenarioCard/PersonaCard at both editor entry points

evidence: src/App.tsx:229-238 and src/components/Library.tsx:130-138 both do `card.rawData as LoreBook` / `as ScriptCard` / `as ScenarioCard` / `as PersonaCard` with no shape check.

src/types/index.ts LibraryCard.rawData carries the comment 'present when cardType is lorebook | script | scenario' but persona cards also store there, so the documented invariant is already out of date.

MCP create_lorebook builds entries with no `id`, while src/types/index.ts LoreEntry declares `id: string` required and LoreBookEditor keys selection (`initialBook?.entries[0]?.id`), deleteEntry and updateEntry on it. LoreBookEditor already owns a normaliser, parseSillyTavernLorebook, that mints ids — but it is only reached from file import, not from these two paths.
detail.suggestion: Route both editor entry points through LoreBookEditor's existing parseSillyTavernLorebook (export it) rather than casting, and give the script/scenario/persona cases the same one-line normalisation; update the rawData comment to include persona.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: bridge bodyOf() declares Record<string, string> for a body containing arrays and objects

evidence: src/lib/bridge/client.ts:291 `if (c.cardType === "character") return c.cardData?.data as unknown as Record<string, string>;` — TavernCardV2Data has `tags: string[]`, `alternate_greetings: string[]` and `extensions: Record<string, unknown>`.
The lie propagates: updateCard spreads the result into `merged` and then casts it back with `as Record<string, unknown>` before handing it to persist().
detail.suggestion: Declare bodyOf as `Record<string, unknown> | undefined` and read the one string field summarise needs with a local narrowing (`typeof body?.character_version === "string" ? … : undefined`). That drops the double cast in updateCard as well.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: personaLlm module doc promises a keyword-parser fallback on failure; the code throws instead

evidence: src/lib/personaLlm/index.ts header: 'Anything that still goes wrong falls back to the keyword parser rather than failing the user's paste.'

sortPersonaWithAi throws 'The model didn't return usable JSON…' when coerceJson returns null, and runWebLlm/runEndpoint throw on missing WebGPU, unreachable endpoint, redirect, or non-ok status. The only fallback in the module is the empty-input case (`if (!text) return parsePersonaText(raw)`).
src/components/SmartImportPanel.tsx runSort catches and surfaces the message; nothing re-runs the parser.
detail.suggestion: Either reword the header to match reality ('failures surface as errors that point the user at Quick sort') or, if the fallback is wanted, wrap the backend call in sortPersonaWithAi so a thrown error returns parsePersonaText(raw) with an explanatory note prepended. The doc edit is the smaller change and matches the error strings, which already say 'Try Quick sort'.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: Three of eight convertTo* functions return TavernCardV2 while the rest return Record<string, unknown>, forcing casts in the dispatcher

evidence: convertToSillyTavern, convertToChub and convertToRisu are typed `(card: TavernCardV2) => TavernCardV2`; convertToJanitorAI, convertToAgnai, convertToVenus, convertToBackyard and convertToGeneric are typed `=> Record<string, unknown>`.
convertCardTo consequently carries `as unknown as Record<string, unknown>` on exactly those three arms (lines 180, 182, 186) while the other five need no cast.
detail.suggestion: Declare all eight as `=> Record<string, unknown>` (a TavernCardV2 already satisfies it structurally once the return type is widened at the declaration), removing the three double casts in convertCardTo. Callers that specifically need the v2 shape can keep using convertToChub/convertToRisu's concrete input.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: Three localStorage readers declare concrete return types over an unvalidated JSON.parse

evidence: src/lib/personaLlm/settings.ts getSorterSettings declares `SorterSettings` and returns `{ ...DEFAULTS, ...JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) ?? "{}") }` — a stored `{"backend": 42}` is returned as a SorterSettings and reaches the backend switch in sortPersonaWithAi.
src/lib/settings.ts loadStoredSettings has the same shape over AppSettings.

src/lib/customTemplates/index.ts load() declares `CustomTemplate[]` but returns whatever JSON.parse yields — a stored object rather than an array is handed back as an array and `[...templates, tpl]` then throws in saveCustomTemplate.
detail.suggestion: In customTemplates load(), guard the one case that actually breaks: `const v = JSON.parse(...); return Array.isArray(v) ? v : [];`. For the two settings readers, either accept the looseness deliberately with a short comment, or coerce the handful of enum-ish keys (backend, and the three booleans) against their defaults.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: safeImageSrc returns null for one class of bad input and throws for another

evidence: src/lib/bridge/client.ts safeImageSrc: `if (typeof src !== "string" || !src) return null;` then `if (!/^data:image\/…/.test(src)) throw new Error(…)`. A caller reading the signature `(src: unknown) => string | null` has no signal that some inputs abort the whole cards.create RPC.
The name reads as a sanitiser (return the safe value, drop the rest), which is the opposite of the throwing branch's behaviour.
detail.suggestion: Rename to `requireInlineImageSrc` and document the throw in a one-line JSDoc, so the throwing branch is visible from the call site in createCard. Behaviour should stay as is — refusing a remote URL loudly is the point.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::brid.summary: Bridge handshake HMACs both directions identically, so a proof can be reflected to bypass the token check

evidence: protocol.ts:70 `proveToken(token, message)` is the only proof primitive and tags nothing about direction; the challenge proof is HMAC(token, clientNonce) and the auth proof is HMAC(token, serverNonce), drawn from the same function and key.

mcp/src/bridge.ts:160 replies to any unauthenticated `hello` with `hmac(clientNonce)` where clientNonce is fully attacker-chosen, and bridge.ts:165 accepts `proofsMatch(msg.proof, hmac(serverNonce))`. Opening two sockets and feeding connection A's serverNonce as connection B's clientNonce yields a valid auth proof without the token.

The header comment at bridge.ts:24-29 states a connection is only promoted 'after it proves knowledge of the shared token', and bridge.ts:80-82 deliberately admits non-browser clients that send no Origin so 'the handshake can still gate them' — the gate that does not hold.
detail.suggestion: Add domain separation so the two proofs cannot substitute for each other: make the challenge proof `proveToken(token, "server:" + clientNonce)` and the auth proof `proveToken(token, "client:" + serverNonce)`, changing the same two call sites in mcp/src/bridge.ts (160, 165) and src/lib/bridge/client.ts (183, 196), and bump BRIDGE_PROTOCOL_VERSION to 3 so an old peer fails the version check rather than the proof check.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::file.summary: Four editors rebuild outputFileName from the card name on every keystroke, discarding a filename the user typed

evidence: LoreBookEditor.tsx:111-114 (and ScriptEditor.tsx:43-46, ScenarioEditor.tsx:46-49, PersonaEditor.tsx:47-50) run `setOutputFileName(...)` in a useEffect keyed on the card name, unconditionally.

Each of those four components renders an editable filename input wired to `setOutputFileName` (LoreBookEditor.tsx:399, ScriptEditor.tsx:158, ScenarioEditor.tsx:165, PersonaEditor.tsx:170), so the next character typed into Name silently discards what the user entered.

src/App.tsx:71-78 solves exactly this for the character editor with a `fileNameTouched` flag whose comment says the effect 'would silently throw their filename away' — the guard exists but was not carried to the sibling editors.
detail.suggestion: Add the same `fileNameTouched` boolean to each of the four editors: set it true in the filename input's onChange and early-return from the name-sync effect when it is set, mirroring src/App.tsx:71-78. If the flag proves identical in all five places, lift it into a small `useDerivedFileName(name, suffix)` hook in src/hooks/ and call it from all five.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::lore.summary: PNG-import and library-load paths cast raw lorebook JSON to LoreBook, skipping the entries normaliser

evidence: LoreBookEditor.tsx:50-87 `parseSillyTavernLorebook` exists precisely because 'ST entries can be an object keyed by numeric strings OR a plain array' (comment at line 48) and it also assigns each entry a `crypto.randomUUID()` id.
ImportPNG.tsx:132, DecodePNG.tsx:116 and Library.tsx:132 pass `parsed as LoreBook` / `card.rawData as LoreBook` straight to the editor with no call to that normaliser.

ImportPNG.tsx:126-130 counts entries via `Object.keys(parsed.entries).length` when they are object-shaped, so that shape demonstrably reaches line 132 and is then cast to an array. The editor's `book.entries.map(...)` (LoreBookEditor.tsx:313) throws on it, and even for array-shaped ST books the entries carry no `id`, so `find((e) => e.id === selectedId)` (line 234) and the React keys are broken.
detail.suggestion: Export `parseSillyTavernLorebook` from a shared module (e.g. src/lib/lorebook.ts) and call it at every entry point into the editor — ImportPNG.tsx:132, DecodePNG.tsx:116, Library.tsx:132 — instead of casting, so the editor only ever receives array-shaped, id-bearing entries. Alternatively normalise once inside LoreBookEditor when `initialBook` is adopted, which removes the cast from all three call sites.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::sile.summary: Card-type dispatch in Library.handleEdit and App.openCard falls through silently when the payload slot is empty

evidence: Library.tsx:127-140 chains `else if (type === "script" && card.rawData)` etc. and has no final else; a record whose rawData/cardData is missing makes the Edit click do nothing, with no status message.

App.tsx:224-243 has the same hole in the bridge's `openCard` switch — `case "character": if (card.cardData) …` and no else — so an agent's `app.open` call reports success over the bridge while nothing opens.
Both files elsewhere use the useStatusMessage/setStatus channel for user-visible failures, so the silence here is inconsistent with the surrounding convention rather than deliberate.
detail.suggestion: Give both dispatches a terminal else that surfaces the failure: in Library.handleEdit call the existing status setter with something like `Cannot open "${card.name}" — its ${type} data is missing or damaged.`, and in App.tsx's openCard log or surface the same rather than returning silently.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::unre.summary: SortOptions.signal is threaded through to fetch but never supplied by any caller, so the cancel path is dead

evidence: personaLlm/index.ts:279 declares `signal?: AbortSignal`, line 296 forwards `opts.signal` to runEndpoint, and line 367 passes it into fetch.

A repo-wide grep for `signal` across src and mcp/src finds no production call site that constructs an AbortController or passes one; SmartImportPanel.tsx:104 calls `sorter(raw, { settings, target, onProgress })` with no signal.
SmartImportPanel.tsx:99-111 sets a `busy` state with no cancel affordance, so a slow endpoint sort cannot be abandoned even though the plumbing for it exists.
detail.suggestion: Decide one way: either wire it up — hold an AbortController ref in SmartImportPanel, pass `controller.signal` at line 104 and render a Cancel button that calls `abort()` — or delete `signal` from SortOptions and the two forwarding parameters so the option does not advertise a capability the app never uses.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::max_.summary: MAX_PAYLOAD comment claims a one-megabyte bound but the constant is four megabytes

evidence: mcp/src/bridge.ts:45-46: `/** Card bodies are text; a megabyte is generous and bounds a hostile peer. */` sits directly above `const MAX_PAYLOAD = 4 * 1024 * 1024;`.

The value is the limit fed to `new WebSocketServer({ maxPayload })` at line 78, i.e. the actual bound against a hostile local peer, so the comment misstates a security-relevant number a reader would otherwise trust without checking.
detail.suggestion: Change the comment to name the real bound — `/** Card bodies are text; 4 MB is generous and bounds a hostile peer. */` — or drop MAX_PAYLOAD to `1024 * 1024` if one megabyte was the intended limit.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::carr.summary: getCarrierPng documents that it never throws, but both of its non-trivial branches can reject

evidence: carrierImage.ts:41-42: 'Never throws for a merely-unsupported format.'

Line 47 calls `base64ToBytes(imageSrc.split(",")[1] ?? "")` for any `data:image/png` src; `atob` throws InvalidCharacterError on a percent-encoded or truncated payload rather than falling back to MINIMAL_PNG.

Line 50 returns `imageSrcToPngBytes(imageSrc)`, whose promise rejects with 'Could not read the image' (line 29) or 'Could not convert the image to PNG' (line 25) whenever the browser cannot decode the data URL — precisely the unsupported-format case the doc excludes.
detail.suggestion: Make the code match the doc: wrap the two branches so a decode failure returns MINIMAL_PNG instead of rejecting (`try { return base64ToBytes(...) } catch { return MINIMAL_PNG }` and `.catch(() => MINIMAL_PNG)` on imageSrcToPngBytes). If exporting should fail loudly instead, delete the 'Never throws' sentence — the five callers already wrap it in try/catch.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::card_t.summary: The five card-type values are redeclared as six separate types plus three literal arrays, bridged by `as` casts

evidence: LibraryCardType (src/types/index.ts:163), CardShape (src/lib/cardShape.ts:13) and CardType (src/lib/bridge/protocol.ts:97) are byte-identical unions declared in three modules.

NonCharType (src/components/DecodePNG.tsx:13) is the same union minus "character"; ALLOWED_CARD_TYPES (src/lib/bridge/client.ts:350) and the z.enum at mcp/src/index.ts:81 restate the values again as data.
CHARACTER_KEYS is exported from src/lib/cardShape.ts:16 and independently re-declared at src/components/DecodePNG.tsx:11.
Because the unions are structurally equal but nominally separate, src/lib/bridge/client.ts uses `as CardType` at lines 281, 312, 360, 367 and 374 to move values between them; nothing checks these.
detail.suggestion: Keep one declaration. Export `const CARD_TYPES = ["character","lorebook","script","scenario","persona"] as const` and `type CardType = typeof CARD_TYPES[number]` from src/lib/bridge/protocol.ts (already shared by both packages), then re-export it as LibraryCardType/CardShape rather than redeclaring, derive ALLOWED_CARD_TYPES and the MCP z.enum from CARD_TYPES, replace NonCharType with Exclude<CardType, "character">, and import CHARACTER_KEYS in DecodePNG.tsx. The five `as CardType` casts in bridge/client.ts then delete themselves.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::decode.summary: decodeCharaFromPng returns `key: string | null` although it only ever emits a MetadataKey, forcing casts in both consumers

evidence: src/lib/pngMetadata/index.ts:128 holds `const knownKeys = ["chara", ...]` as an untyped string[] in a module that already imports MetadataKey (line 1) and uses it for the encode direction (line 192).

foundKey is only assigned inside `if (!foundJson && knownKeys.includes(keyword))` (line 162), so the return value is provably a MetadataKey, yet the signature at line 117 declares `key: string | null`.

Consumers pay for the lost narrowing: src/components/DecodePNG.tsx:80 and 190-194 write `result.key as NonCharType` even after guarding with `key in NON_CHAR_META`, and shapeForKey (src/lib/cardShape.ts:19) has to accept a bare string and re-test the literals.
detail.suggestion: Type the array as `const KNOWN_KEYS: readonly MetadataKey[] = [...]` (or derive both from a single const tuple) and change decodeCharaFromPng's return to `key: MetadataKey | null`. `key in NON_CHAR_META` then narrows on its own and the three `as NonCharType` casts in DecodePNG.tsx can go.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::bodyof.summary: bridge/client.ts bodyOf() is annotated Record<string, string> but returns objects holding arrays and nested records

evidence: src/lib/bridge/client.ts:289-292: `function bodyOf(c: LibraryCard): Record<string, string> | undefined` reaches its value through `c.cardData?.data as unknown as Record<string, string>`.

The real type there is TavernCardV2Data, whose members include alternate_greetings: string[], tags: string[], character_book?: CharacterBook and extensions: Record<string, unknown> — none of which are strings.
The non-character branch is worse: `c.rawData as Record<string, string> | undefined` re-labels an `unknown` that holds arbitrary lorebook/script/scenario bodies.
The falsehood is not inert: updateCard (line 365) spreads bodyOf(existing) into the merge and then has to cast it back with `merged as Record<string, unknown>` to pass it on.
detail.suggestion: Change bodyOf's return type to Record<string, unknown> | undefined — that is what the data actually is, it removes the `as unknown as` double cast and the compensating cast at line 365, and summarise()'s two reads only need a typeof check on character_version and version.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::lorebo.summary: `parsed as LoreBook` on the PNG and library paths bypasses the only code that normalises SillyTavern's object-keyed entries

evidence: parseSillyTavernLorebook (src/components/LoreBookEditor.tsx:50) exists precisely because ST entries can be an object keyed by numeric strings or a plain array, and it also fills in every missing field.
It is called from exactly one place — the drag-a-JSON-file handler at line 152.

The PNG import path asserts instead: src/components/ImportPNG.tsx:132 `onLoadLorebook?.(parsed as LoreBook, imageSrc)` on a value straight out of JSON.parse; src/components/DecodePNG.tsx:116 does the same; the library path does `card.rawData as LoreBook` at src/App.tsx:229 and src/components/Library.tsx:132.

LoreBookEditor then trusts the annotation immediately — line 97 reads `initialBook?.entries[0]?.id` and lines 128-142 call .find/.map on book.entries — so an object-shaped `entries` reaching the editor by PNG is a runtime failure the type system was told could not happen.
detail.suggestion: Export parseSillyTavernLorebook from a lib module (e.g. src/lib/loreBook.ts) and run every inbound lorebook through it: replace `parsed as LoreBook` in ImportPNG.tsx/DecodePNG.tsx and `card.rawData as LoreBook` in App.tsx/Library.tsx with parseSillyTavernLorebook(parsed). That makes the LoreBook annotation earned on all three routes instead of one.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::librar.summary: LibraryCard keeps its cardType/cardData/rawData invariant in comments, so ~10 call sites re-assert it by hand

evidence: src/types/index.ts:184-186 documents the rule in trailing comments: `cardData?: TavernCardV2;   // present when cardType === "character"` and `rawData?: unknown;  // present when cardType is lorebook | script | scenario`.

Every consumer therefore switches on cardType and asserts the payload itself — src/App.tsx:229-238 (four `as` casts), src/components/Library.tsx:132-138 (four more), plus `card.rawData as { version?: string } | null` at Library.tsx:20 and the bodyOf branch at src/lib/bridge/client.ts:290-291.
src/lib/library/index.ts:88-90 also treats cardType as possibly absent (`c.cardType ?? "character"`) despite the field being declared required.
detail.suggestion: Split LibraryCard into a discriminated union over cardType — { cardType: "character"; cardData: TavernCardV2 } | { cardType: "lorebook"; rawData: LoreBook } | ... sharing a LibraryCardBase for the common id/name/tags/timestamp fields. Narrowing on card.cardType then supplies the payload type at all eight App.tsx/Library.tsx sites and the casts disappear rather than being replaced by anything.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::lorebo.summary: parseSillyTavernLorebook takes `any`, so its `const scan_depth: number = raw.scan_depth ?? 50` annotations are unchecked

evidence: src/components/LoreBookEditor.tsx:50 `function parseSillyTavernLorebook(raw: any): LoreBook`, and line 70 `rawEntries.map((e: any) => ...)`.

Lines 51-58 annotate each extraction — `const scan_depth: number = raw.scan_depth ?? 50`, `const recursive_scanning: boolean = raw.recursive_scanning ?? false` — but because raw is `any`, a card storing "50" or "true" passes straight through under a number/boolean annotation.

The entry mapper is looser still: keys and secondary_keys get Array.isArray guards, but content, insertion_order and priority are taken with a bare `??`, so a numeric content lands in a field typed string.
detail.suggestion: Change the parameter to `unknown`, narrow once (const r = (raw && typeof raw === "object" ? raw : {}) as Record<string, unknown>), and pull the per-field coercions through the same String()/Number() style that src/lib/platforms/converters.ts already uses on foreign card JSON. The eslint-disable comments then go away with the `any`.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::bridge.summary: Inbound bridge RPC params are cast, not checked, and callApp<T> lets each caller name any result type

evidence: src/lib/bridge/client.ts:260-271 dispatches with `req.params as ListParams`, `as GetParams`, `as CreateParams`, `as UpdateParams`, `as DeleteParams`, `as OpenParams` — the protocol declares params as `unknown` (protocol.ts:117) precisely because it arrives over a socket.
Only createCard validates anything (ALLOWED_CARD_TYPES at line 351); getCard/updateCard/removeCard/openCard trust params.id to be a string, and listCards trusts params.type to be a CardType.

On the other side, mcp/src/bridge.ts:230 `callApp<T = unknown>(method: BridgeMethod, params?: unknown)` ties neither params nor result to the method, so callApp<GetResult>("cards.get", {}) type-checks.
The protocol module already names a params and a result interface for every method, so the information needed to check this exists and is simply not connected.
detail.suggestion: In protocol.ts add one mapped type — interface BridgeCalls { "cards.get": { params: GetParams; result: GetResult }; ... } — and type callApp as callApp<M extends BridgeMethod>(method: M, params: BridgeCalls[M]["params"]): Promise<BridgeCalls[M]["result"]>. That removes the explicit <T> from every MCP call site. On the app side, guard the two fields that matter (typeof p?.id === "string", type against ALLOWED_CARD_TYPES) before dispatch rather than asserting.

flat_dirs::src/lib.reasoning: The detector counts child directories toward the overload total, but those child directories are exactly the domain partition it recommends. The remaining root files are small high-fan-in leaf utilities that the rubric explicitly says to skip.

732099ceb6f84e0a.reasoning: 649 lines with one responsibility — turn a text blob into card fields. Four strategies are separate named functions tried in order from a three-line entry point, and the vocabulary is data (LABEL_ALIASES, JSON_KEY_MAP, the three keyword lists) rather than branches. Splitting it would scatter one decision across files. This is the rubric's explicit skip case.

b2d1b32542458590.reasoning: The cyclomatic hotspot is the ws message handler, which is a two-phase protocol state machine (hello/auth, then RPC responses) with section-header comments marking the phases. Its state — authed, serverNonce, handshakeTimer — is per-connection and genuinely belongs in the connection closure; hoisting it would require inventing a connection object to hold what the closure already holds. Nesting is inherent to the problem.

c595d5aab9377ca6.reasoning: The branching is two backends (runWebLlm, runEndpoint) behind one entry point, each a single focused function, with schema, prompts and result shaping all derived from FIELD_DOCS/TARGET_FIELDS rather than restated per target. coerceJson and toParsedPersona are separate and small. No responsibility is mixed in.
